svg.title: SQL Server and Cosmos DB, side by side: the same application on Azure SQL Database (left) and Azure Cosmos DB (right), row by row
svg.text: SQL Server and Cosmos DB, side by side: one application, two stores, the same rows

Read across. Each row is a question a developer who knows one of these and not the other asks first; each box names the file in this repository that answers it, and each number is one a record measured.
Azure SQL Database
The live site's default store: https://theyard.stevenstout.biz
Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL
The second site's default store: https://theyard-cosmos.stevenstout.biz
What it is
the model each engine enforces
A relational database
Azure SQL Database, General Purpose serverless, the free limit (ADR-039)
Tables, rows, foreign keys and T-SQL. The schema is the contract and the
engine enforces it: a row that breaks a constraint is refused before it lands.
The server sits one region away from the container, which is the fact behind
most of the numbers below.
A document database
Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL, account cosmos-theyard-ss, free tier (ADR-059)
JSON documents in containers, each container split by a partition key. The
document owns its shape; the engine enforces the key, the id and the etag, and
nothing else.
The account is in the container's own region, so a round trip is milliseconds,
not tens of them.
How the application reaches it
the adapter behind the same three ports
Entity Framework Core over SqlClient
api/TheYard.Infrastructure/YardConnection.cs, EfSources.cs, SqlLogInterceptor.cs
A DbContext per request, LINQ that EF turns into statements, and a managed
identity token instead of a password. The interceptor records every statement,
parameters by name and never a value (ADR-043).
The Cosmos DB SDK, directly
api/TheYard.Infrastructure.Cosmos/CosmosStore.cs, CosmosSources.cs
One CosmosClient for the process, point reads and queries by hand, so the
request charge and the diagnostics stay visible. Managed identity with a
data-plane role; local authentication is disabled, so no key exists to leak
A bid, at rest
the same fact, stored two ways
One row in dbo.Bids
api/TheYard.Database/Tables/Bids.sql
PRIMARY KEY (UserId, VehicleId). A FOREIGN KEY to AspNetUsers with ON DELETE
CASCADE, so deleting an account takes its bids. A rowversion column the engine
maintains, so a lost update is impossible to write by accident.
One document in the bids container
infra/cosmos/bids.json, partition key /user_id
id is the vehicle, the partition is the buyer, so every write is a point write
inside one partition. The etag is the concurrency token. No foreign key
exists; the code keeps that rule, and the indexing policy excludes every path
because nothing queries them.
Writing a bid
read, decide, write, and what happens when two writers race
Find, then Add or update, then SaveChanges
api/TheYard.Infrastructure/EfSources.cs, region bid-store
Two statements. A DbUpdateConcurrencyException means another writer moved the
row between the read and the write; the store starts again from what is there
now, three tries, then the exception travels.
measured from the container: 84 ms, 2 statements (ADR-067)
Point read, then CreateItem or ReplaceItem with If-Match
api/TheYard.Infrastructure.Cosmos/CosmosSources.cs, region cosmos-bid-store
Two operations. A 412 is the same race as the concurrency exception and a 409
is a create that lost; the same three tries. The read costs 1 RU, the create
5.52, the replace 10.29.
measured from the container: 10 ms, 2 operations, 6.52 RU (ADR-067)
Keeping an address unique
the guarantee one engine gives and the other has to be built
A unique index does it
api/TheYard.Database/Tables/Identity/AspNetUsers.sql, UserNameIndex
The address is the user name here, and the unique index on NormalizedUserName
refuses a second account with the same one. Nothing in the application has to
remember to check.
A claim document does it
api/TheYard.Infrastructure.Cosmos/CosmosUserStore.cs, region create
No unique index spans partitions. The store creates a document whose id is the
address first; a 409 on that create is the refusal. If the account write then
fails the claim is removed, and a process that dies between the two leaves a
claim with no account, which is the written-down cost of the shape (ADR-061).
Indexes, and what a query costs
where the design work goes on each side
Indexes chosen per query, in the DACPAC
api/TheYard.Database (the SQL project), ADR-040
A clustered primary key, nonclustered indexes where a query needs them, and a
plan the engine picks. The cost of a query is compute time and it shows up as
vCore-seconds against the free limit.
An indexing policy per container, in JSON
infra/cosmos/*.json, ADR-058
Every path indexed by default, and here every path excluded on the four site
containers because they are read by id. The cost of an operation is request
units, charged per call, and the wrong partition key turns a 1 RU read into a
fan-out across every partition.
the experiment: 8.84 RU per seeded document tuned, 16.07 under the default (ADR-058)
Consistency and transactions
how far one write can reach
ACID across tables
one transaction, any number of tables, the engine arbitrates
A transaction can touch every table, row versioning keeps readers off writers,
and the database is the single arbiter of what happened in what order.
Session consistency, atomic inside one partition
TransactionalBatch, one partition key at a time
A reset deletes one buyer's bids as one batch because they share a partition.
Nothing spans partitions atomically; the application is arranged so nothing
needs to.
What the Admin tab shows
the same page on both sites
Every statement, with its time
the SQL card and the console log, category Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Database.Command
The statement, its parameters by name, the milliseconds. On the SQL site the
Timing card's SQL line is the ring these feed (ADR-043).
Every operation, with its charge
the operations card and the console log, category TheYard.Infrastructure.Cosmos.CosmosStore
The operation, the container, the request units, the milliseconds and whether
it named a partition or fanned out. Since 1.0.0.103 each is also one log line
beside the SQL ones (ADR-062).
Measured on this application
twenty paired rounds from Missouri, and the proof from the container itself
The relational side
ADR-064 (the client), ADR-067 (the proof)
From Missouri: bid write 219 ms, sign in 249 ms, register 319 ms at p50. From
the container: 39 ms of every operation is the round trip to a server one
region away.
the proof: on 3 of 8 paths the same time; on the other 5 the difference is the round trip
The document side
ADR-064 (the client), ADR-067 (the proof)
From Missouri: bid write 135 ms, sign in 221 ms, register 216 ms at p50. From
the container: 2 ms round trip, and every sign-in costs exactly 2 RU.
taking one round trip per operation off each side leaves them the same
What it costs this month
both stores at $0.00, read from the meters
The free limit
100,000 vCore-seconds and 32 GB a month, renewing, ADR-039
Serverless compute that auto-pauses when nobody visits, so the first request
after a quiet stretch waits for it to wake (a 25 s health check was measured
once). The cost so far is $0.00.
The free tier
1000 RU/s and 25 GB for the life of the account, ADR-059
Shared across the database's containers, never paused, and the site's whole
month is pennies of it at serverless rates. The store costs $0.00; the second
container group that serves it is about $34 a month at list.
The records behind the left column: ADR-039 The SQL Server backend, ADR-040 Data first, and the database in source control, ADR-041 Two providers and a SQL project, explained, ADR-043 What
the database is actually doing. Behind the right: ADR-058 The partition key, ADR-059 A second store on Cosmos DB, and what it costs, ADR-060 The ports learn to wait, ADR-061 Accounts on a
document store, ADR-062 What the store is actually doing.
Across both: ADR-063 Backends, side by side; ADR-064 Measuring both stores; ADR-065 Cosmos DB, explained for someone who knows SQL Server; ADR-066 One container, both stores; ADR-067 Same
performance, proven; ADR-069 A permanent address for the second site.
Both container groups open both stores; each site serves its default and the Store bar links to the other at the same page. A measurement can name the other store for one request with the
X-Yard-Store header.
Source: docs/images/sql-vs-cosmos.svg in the repository, drawn by docs/images/sql-vs-cosmos.mjs and redrawn when a store, a file or a number changes.
